newsitem.title: NORWAY: Taxman upholds 2.2 bln NOK ruling on DnB.
newsitem.headline: Taxman upholds 2.2 bln NOK ruling on DnB.

text.p: Norwegian tax authorities have upheld a ruling ordering Den norske Bank (DnB) to reduce its overall tax-loss carried forward by 2.20 billion crowns for 1993, an Oslo bourse statement said on Thursday.
The amount corresponds to a write-down of preference capital in 1993 received by DnB, Norway's top commercial bank, from the Commercial Banks' Guarantee Fund. DnB had appealed against the decision.

The November 1995 tax decision which now was upheld means that DnB will start paying taxes earlier than foreseen after being rescued by the government from a financial crisis around 1990, according to analysts.
DnB spokesman Jarl Veggan said however it was unclear when the bank's income would become taxable.
"The question depends on our annual results," he said.
DnB in August booked net profits of 1.51 billion crowns, down from 1.67 billion in the first half of 1995.

"Before this ruling came, at the end of 1995 the DnB group had 3.9 billion crowns in tax losses carried forward, including 1.5 billion for DnB ASA," Veggan told Reuters. "It is not clear yet if we will get into a tax position this year."

Last month tax authorities announced they may propose to amend the 1994 and 1995 tax returns of DnB as well to increase its taxable income by 1.1 billion crowns. The bank has said it would fight such a decision.
Authorities have said they may question the breakdown of tax deductions on the paying of interest on debts between the bank's business in Norway and abroad.
Group managing director Finn Hvistendahl has said the bank would probably have to start paying taxes this year should it lose all tax cases.
